summary: Root cause of user's 'preview not showing' localized: Redis and PostgreSQL were NOT running in the container. Backend was up but every /api/v1 request that touched Redis (all auth endpoints) returned 500, and Postgres user/db/schema did not exist. After starting redis-server + postgresql, creating the 'housing' user/db, running `alembic upgrade head`, and re-seeding the Platform Owner (mobile 9999999999), the full OTP login flow works end-to-end. Frontend loads at the external preview URL and renders the login and signup pages correctly.

critical.issue: redis-server was not running. All OTP endpoints returned 500 ('Connection refused connecting to localhost:6379'). Fixed by `service redis-server start`.
PostgreSQL was not running and the `housing` role + `housing` db did not exist. Fixed by starting postgresql, creating role/db, and running `alembic upgrade head`.
Seeded Platform Owner (mobile 9999999999) was missing from DB after fresh migrations. Recreated via `python -m scripts.seed_platform_owner --mobile 9999999999 --name 'Platform Owner'`.

minor.issue: Accepts obviously invalid mobile numbers (e.g. '123') and returns 200. No length/format validation on the Pydantic model — should be exactly 10 digits.

Exposed at app root without the /api prefix, so it is not reachable through the Kubernetes ingress (which only routes /api/*). Health probes from outside cannot hit it. Consider mounting it as /api/health as well.
SQLAlchemy `echo=True` appears enabled — backend logs are extremely noisy with full SQL dumps on every request. Should be disabled outside of DEBUG.

action_items: Make redis + postgres start automatically (supervisor entry) so this container doesn't silently break auth on every restart — this is the actual RCA of the user's 'preview nhi dikh rha hai' report.
Add mobile-number validation (regex ^[0-9]{10}$) to /api/v1/auth/otp/request request model.
Expose health at /api/health (in addition to /health) so ingress-level probes work.
Turn off SQLAlchemy echo in non-debug environments.
critical_code_review_comments: Auth service depends on Redis but the container had no autostart for redis/postgres — a single container restart takes the whole app down with 500s. Add these to supervisor or a boot script.
OTP request endpoint has no input validation on `mobile` (accepts '123'), which increases abuse surface and Redis key pollution.
`/health` is not under `/api` so external LB probes cannot reach it through ingress.
SQLAlchemy `echo=True` is on by default in this env — leaks queries + parameters into logs.

Health is at /health (NOT reachable through ingress; only /api/* is proxied). To run OTP tests: `redis-cli --scan --pattern 'otp:*' | xargs -r redis-cli del` then generate OTP via subprocess with REDIS_URL=redis://localhost:6379/0 and DATABASE_URL=postgresql+asyncpg://housing:housing@localhost:5432/housing (the repo's tests/conftest.py forces DB 15 + a test DB via os.environ.setdefault — that's why /app/tests/test_smoke.py lives OUTSIDE /app/backend/tests to bypass that conftest). Run with `pytest /app/tests/test_smoke.py -v`. Redis and Postgres must be running — they do NOT autostart on container boot.
rca of the issue: User reported preview not loading. Frontend actually serves 200. Real breakage was backend-side: every /api/v1/auth/* call returned {"detail":"Internal server error"} because redis-server was down (Errno 111 Connection refused to localhost:6379). Additionally postgresql was down and even after start had no `housing` role/db. Steps to reproduce before fix: `curl -X POST $URL/api/v1/auth/otp/request -d '{"mobile":"9999999999"}' -H 'Content-Type: application/json'` → 500. Backend log: `redis.exceptions.ConnectionError`. Mitigation applied: (1) `service redis-server start`; (2) `service postgresql start`; (3) `psql -c "CREATE USER housing WITH PASSWORD 'housing' CREATEDB; CREATE DATABASE housing OWNER housing;"`; (4) `alembic upgrade head`; (5) `python -m scripts.seed_platform_owner --mobile 9999999999 --name 'Platform Owner'`. Post-fix: OTP request → 200, OTP verify → JWT tokens issued, `/api/v1/societies` accessible with bearer. Long-term fix (main agent): add redis + postgres to supervisor autostart.
